correctness.rationale: The uniform-seed event equals an exact nonnegative Bernstein-basis sum over all retained-edge subsets. The checker enumerates all labelled Prüfer trees of orders two through five and all thresholds, certifying an edge with integer coefficients no larger than any competitor in each of 555 exhaustive cases. Complete six-vertex exact coefficient enumerations yield all five polynomial identities, strict exclusion of other edges, and the unique rational switching threshold 3/5; these establish the continuum of p, not a finite-grid inference. Replaying the provided checker is required for reproduction. No claims for larger orders or dependent transmissions.

originality.rationale: The precise smallest-order claim is not implied by the inspected independent-bond model definitions, by expected-infections optimization, or by deterministic worst-case component-size edge deletion. Full primary textual comparisons were made for the closest methods. Exact generic reliability treatments remain a priority risk, so novelty is best knowledge within the investigated evidence, not proof of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: Uninspected exact network-reliability/edge-vitality tables could encode the six-vertex comparison or a stronger small-order result.
The small-graph minimum is restricted to independent bond transmissions; the SIR literature with dependent transmissions is not an equivalent model.

value.rationale: Preventive network edge choice under an explicit large-outbreak chance constraint is a natural risk-sensitive alternative to minimizing the mean. The finding supplies a sharp smallest network that forces a change in best preemptive cut with transmissibility, a complete exclusion through five vertices, and a simple exact six-vertex threshold; all three facts are operationally interpretable as a finite-network benchmark, independently of any field validation.
